name: dpi
title: DPI Bypass
description: The `dpi` script's censorship bypass as a toggle with an indicator: Turn on / Turn off, a Repair row when only half of it is in effect, the status with its facts, an end-to-end test whose rows land one by one, the log and the build. A shield on the bar while it is on, amber while partial. byedpi and the network settings on macOS, zapret and dnscrypt-proxy under systemd on Linux; the script does all of it, pal runs it and draws what it says.
author: pal

settings.label: Tool
settings.description: The dpi script: a name on PATH or a path. It lives at ~/.local/bin/dpi; that directory is looked in when the name is not on PATH.

settings.label: Test urls
settings.description: What the test curls: `url`, or `url = blocked` (the bypass must get it through) / `url = control` (a site that must keep working). Without a role the first two are blocked and the rest controls, as the script's list reads.

settings.label: Override DNS
settings.description: The resolvers `dpi on` sets on macOS (the script's DNS_ON), so the status can tell a full bypass from a partial one: the proxy up with the DNS still the ISP's is partial. Empty: DNS is not judged.

store.tagline: The dpi bypass on and off, with a shield on the bar
features: Turn on bypass / Turn off bypass leads the palette and sits in the root's Now section while on; Enter runs the script, the panel hides and the HUD says what the script said (`dpi on (Wi-Fi -> socks5://127.0.0.1:1080, dns 1.1.1.1 9.9.9.9)`)
A partial state (the proxy up but the SOCKS or the DNS not pointing at it, or the reverse; one of the two Linux units down) is amber with the reason and gets a Repair row: off, then on
The status row's detail pane: proxy, service, DNS and SOCKS (the units and the DNS probe on Linux); Enter copies the script's own output

The test: one curl per url at once, through the proxy while it is up, each row landing as it answers with the code as a coloured tag, the time and its role; the header says `2 blocked reach, 4 controls fine` or names what failed; `cmd+r` runs it again

The bar item: a shield while on, hidden while off by its rule (`show = "always"` keeps a muted one), amber while partial; the popover has the status card, Enter toggles, `t` runs the test in place, `r` repairs, `l` opens the log, `o` the palette
Linux: `sudo -n true` is probed before a switch; a closed credential window is a toast saying to run `sudo -v` first, never a hung prompt
Nothing of byedpi or the network settings is reimplemented: the script is the engine, pal is the button and the light
